% \vsize sweep of combined_document.tex: the same
% document at \vsize=2.5in (MiKTeX baseline), so the page-break choice over
% display, \halign and paragraph penalties is pinned at more than one
% goal height.  Body identical to combined_document.tex.
% comprehensive fixture (FR-1) — realistic combined document.
% One end-user-style plain TeX document that interleaves ALL of the delivered
% math + alignment constructs across >=2 natural pages (no \eject), so the
% page-builder decisions interact with the mixed content.  Every construct is
% already individually byte-exact vs MiKTeX (math_inline, alignment_text,
% alignment_matrix, alignment_eqalign, short-skip); this fixture pins
% them COMBINED against a MiKTeX baseline within the tolerance
% (+/-0.5pt V / +/-0.1pt H).
%
% Constructs exercised: running text; inline $...$ in prose (2+ paragraphs);
% a $$...$$ display preceded by a SHORT in-paragraph line (the
% \predisplaysize short-skip path); a text \halign; inline $\matrix{}$ and
% $\pmatrix{}$; a display $$\eqalign{}$$.  \vsize is deliberately short so the
% material breaks naturally across >=2 pages.
\hsize=6.5in
\vsize=2.5in
\nopagenumbers
\noindent
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. The identity $x+y=z$ holds
for all values, and $\alpha\beta$ are Greek letters that appear inline in
running prose without disturbing the surrounding line.
\par
\noindent
Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs. When $a$ and $b$ are given, the
sum $a+b$ follows, and the relation $x=y$ closes the argument for this
second paragraph of ordinary body text.
\par
\noindent
The system
$$\eqalign{x &= y + z\cr a &= b\cr}$$
has a solution when the coefficients agree.
\par
\noindent
A small table of pairs follows to mix alignment with the surrounding prose:
\par
\normalbaselines
\halign{#\hfil&\quad#\hfil\cr
  one&two\cr
  three&four\cr
  five&six\cr}
\par
\noindent
Inline matrices also appear in text: a matrix $\matrix{a&b\cr c&d\cr}$ and a
parenthesised one $\pmatrix{x&y\cr z&w\cr}$ sit within the paragraph, and
enough further running text follows here to push the remaining content onto a
second page so the page-builder must break the mixed body naturally rather
than at a forced boundary.
\par
\noindent
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog once more, and pack my box with
five dozen liquor jugs a final time to fill out the closing page of this
combined verification document.
\par
\bye
